claim: A mass spectrometric method was established for the sensitive and accurate quantification of multiple enzymatic DNA modifications.
source: We established a mass spectrometric method for the sensitive and accurate quantification of multiple enzymatic DNA modifications.
evidence: The abstract directly states this as a methodological achievement of the study.

claim: DNA was isolated from 124 archean, bacterial, fungal, plant, and mammalian species.
source: Then, we isolated DNA from 124 archean, bacterial, fungal, plant, and mammalian species, and several tissues and created a resource of global DNA modification quantities.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the number and types of species analyzed.

claim: Only three DNA modifications (5mdC, N6mdA, and 5hmdC) were detected above a picomolar detection limit across species.
source: We report that only three of the studied DNA modifications, methylcytosine (5mdC), methyladenine (N6mdA) and hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmdC), were detected above a picomolar detection limit across species
evidence: The abstract explicitly reports this finding from the study.

claim: 5mdC dominated in higher eukaryotes.
source: only three of the studied DNA modifications, methylcytosine (5mdC), methyladenine (N6mdA) and hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmdC), were detected above a picomolar detection limit across species, and dominated in higher eukaryotes (5mdC)
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that 5mdC dominated in higher eukaryotes.

claim: N6mdA dominated in bacteria.
source: only three of the studied DNA modifications, methylcytosine (5mdC), methyladenine (N6mdA) and hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmdC), were detected above a picomolar detection limit across species, and dominated in higher eukaryotes (5mdC), in bacteria (N6mdA)
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that N6mdA dominated in bacteria.

claim: 5hmdC dominated in the vertebrate central nervous systems.
source: only three of the studied DNA modifications, methylcytosine (5mdC), methyladenine (N6mdA) and hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmdC), were detected above a picomolar detection limit across species, and dominated in higher eukaryotes (5mdC), in bacteria (N6mdA), or the vertebrate central nervous systems (5hmdC).
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that 5hmdC dominated in vertebrate CNS.

claim: All three modifications (5mdC, N6mdA, and 5hmdC) were detected simultaneously in only one tested species, Raphanus sativus.
source: All three modifications were detected simultaneously in only one of the tested species, Raphanus sativus.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this unique finding for Raphanus sativus.

claim: DNA modifications were either absent or detected only at trace quantities across all yeasts and insect genomes studied.
source: In contrast, these modifications were either absent or detected only at trace quantities, across all yeasts and insect genomes studied.
evidence: The abstract explicitly reports this finding for yeasts and insects.

claim: In Allium cepa, more than 35% of cytosines were methylated.
source: For instance, in Allium cepa, Helianthus annuus, or Andropogon gerardi, more than 35% of cytosines were methylated.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this high methylation level in Allium cepa.

claim: In Helianthus annuus, more than 35% of cytosines were methylated.
source: For instance, in Allium cepa, Helianthus annuus, or Andropogon gerardi, more than 35% of cytosines were methylated.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this high methylation level in Helianthus annuus.

claim: In Andropogon gerardi, more than 35% of cytosines were methylated.
source: For instance, in Allium cepa, Helianthus annuus, or Andropogon gerardi, more than 35% of cytosines were methylated.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this high methylation level in Andropogon gerardi.

claim: 5hmdC was detected in plants like Lepidium sativum.
source: Additionally, next to the mammlian CNS, 5hmdC was also detected in plants like Lepidium sativum
evidence: The abstract explicitly reports detection of 5hmdC in Lepidium sativum.

claim: 5hmdC was found on 8% of cytosines in the Garra barreimiae brain samples.
source: and was found on 8% of cytosines in the Garra barreimiae brain samples.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this quantitative finding for Garra barreimiae.

claim: 5-methyl-2′-deoxycytidine (5mdC) was the first nucleotide modification to be discovered.
source: The methylation of the fifth carbon (C5) of the cytosine ring to yield 5-methyl-2′-deoxycytidine (5mdC) was the first nucleotide modification to be discovered (Hotchkiss, 1948)
evidence: The introduction cites Hotchkiss, 1948 as the source for this historical fact.

claim: 5mdC can be enzymatically oxidized into 5-hydroxymethyl-2′-deoxycytidine (5hmdC).
source: 5mdC can be enzymatically oxidized into 5-hydroxymethyl-2′-deoxycytidine (5hmdC) and further into 5-formyl-2′-deoxycytidine (fdC) and 5-carboxyl-2′-deoxycytidine (cadC) (Hu et al., 2015; Ito et al., 2011; Tahiliani et al., 2009).
evidence: The introduction cites multiple papers supporting this biochemical pathway.

claim: 5hmdC can be further oxidized into 5-formyl-2′-deoxycytidine (fdC).
source: 5mdC can be enzymatically oxidized into 5-hydroxymethyl-2′-deoxycytidine (5hmdC) and further into 5-formyl-2′-deoxycytidine (fdC) and 5-carboxyl-2′-deoxycytidine (cadC) (Hu et al., 2015; Ito et al., 2011; Tahiliani et al., 2009).
evidence: The introduction cites multiple papers supporting this biochemical pathway.

claim: 5hmdC can be further oxidized into 5-carboxyl-2′-deoxycytidine (cadC).
source: 5mdC can be enzymatically oxidized into 5-hydroxymethyl-2′-deoxycytidine (5hmdC) and further into 5-formyl-2′-deoxycytidine (fdC) and 5-carboxyl-2′-deoxycytidine (cadC) (Hu et al., 2015; Ito et al., 2011; Tahiliani et al., 2009).
evidence: The introduction cites multiple papers supporting this biochemical pathway.

claim: 5hmdC has been found to accumulate in the mammalian brain, specifically in the large Purkinje neurons.
source: Although these modifications have been described as transient intermediates of 5mdC demethylation, at least one (5hmdC) has been found to accumulate in the mammalian brain, specifically in the large Purkinje neurons, indicating a regulatory function (Kriaucionis and Heintz, 2009).
evidence: The introduction cites Kriaucionis and Heintz, 2009 for this finding.

claim: N4-methyl-2′-deoxycytidine (4mdC) is found in bacteria.
source: N4-methyl-2′-deoxycytidine (4mdC), found in bacteria, is yet another form of cytosine modification (Janulaitis et al., 1983; Ehrlich et al., 1987).
evidence: The introduction cites two papers supporting the presence of 4mdC in bacteria.

claim: N6-methyl-2′-deoxyadenosine (N6mdA) was initially discovered in bacterial genomes.
source: N6-methyl-2′-deoxyadenosine (N6mdA) was initially discovered in bacterial genomes (Dunn and Smith, 1955)
evidence: The introduction cites Dunn and Smith, 1955 for the initial discovery.

claim: N6mdA was later found in archaea, plants, and nematodes.
source: N6-methyl-2′-deoxyadenosine (N6mdA) was initially discovered in bacterial genomes (Dunn and Smith, 1955) and later also in archaea, plants, and nematodes (Couturier and Lindås, 2018; Liang et al., 2018).
evidence: The introduction cites two papers supporting the later discovery in other organisms.

claim: Arabidopsis thaliana has orders of magnitude higher levels of 5mdC compared to Drosophila melanogaster.
source: For instance, Arabidopsis thaliana has orders of magnitude higher levels 5mdC compared to the dominant insect model Drosophila melanogaster, while the dominant yeast model organism Saccharomyces cerevisiae lacks this modification altogether (Münzel et al., 2011; Capuano et al., 2014).
evidence: The introduction cites two papers supporting this comparison.

claim: Saccharomyces cerevisiae lacks 5mdC modification.
source: For instance, Arabidopsis thaliana has orders of magnitude higher levels 5mdC compared to the dominant insect model Drosophila melanogaster, while the dominant yeast model organism Saccharomyces cerevisiae lacks this modification altogether (Münzel et al., 2011; Capuano et al., 2014).
evidence: The introduction cites two papers supporting this finding.

claim: The LC-MRM method achieves detection limits in picomolar ranges.
source: Combined with the high sensitivity offered by a triple quadrupole mass spectrometer (Agilent 6470), we were able to achieve detection limits in picomolar ranges (Figure 1A).
evidence: The results section states this and references Figure 1A showing the detection limits.

claim: The limit of detection for 5mdC is 4.6 nM.
source: The limits of detection for 5mdC, 5hmdC, and N6mdA are 4.6 nM, 320 pM, and 19 pM, respectively.
evidence: Figure 1 caption explicitly states this detection limit.

claim: The limit of detection for 5hmdC is 320 pM.
source: The limits of detection for 5mdC, 5hmdC, and N6mdA are 4.6 nM, 320 pM, and 19 pM, respectively.
evidence: Figure 1 caption explicitly states this detection limit.

claim: The limit of detection for N6mdA is 19 pM.
source: The limits of detection for 5mdC, 5hmdC, and N6mdA are 4.6 nM, 320 pM, and 19 pM, respectively.
evidence: Figure 1 caption explicitly states this detection limit.

claim: fdC and cadC were not detected at significant levels in any of the genomes measured.
source: First, despite the broad coverage, high sensitivity, and precision of our method, we did not detect significant levels of fdC and cadC in any of the genomes measured (limits of detection were 238 pM and 251 pM, respectively).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: The limit of detection for fdC is 238 pM.
source: First, despite the broad coverage, high sensitivity, and precision of our method, we did not detect significant levels of fdC and cadC in any of the genomes measured (limits of detection were 238 pM and 251 pM, respectively).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this detection limit.

claim: The limit of detection for cadC is 251 pM.
source: First, despite the broad coverage, high sensitivity, and precision of our method, we did not detect significant levels of fdC and cadC in any of the genomes measured (limits of detection were 238 pM and 251 pM, respectively).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this detection limit.

claim: Unicellular fungi studied had hardly any detectable DNA modifications.
source: A notable exception was that we detected hardly any of these DNA modifications in the unicellular fungi studied (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: 5mdC, 5hmdC, and N6mdA are very low if not absent in typical yeast species.
source: Hence it is not merely 5mdC (Capuano et al., 2014; Binz et al., 2018; Nai et al., 2020), but also its oxidized form 5hmdC along with N6mdA that are very low if not absent in typical yeast species.
evidence: The results section states this finding with citations to previous work.

claim: Insects Trichoplusia ni, Spodoptera frugiperda, and Drosophila melanogaster all had DNA modifications at much lower levels compared to higher organisms and bacteria.
source: It is interesting in this context that the insects Trichoplusia ni, Spodoptera frugiperda, and D. melanogaster (Supplementary file 1) all had DNA modifications, but also at much lower levels compared to both, higher organisms but also bacteria.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this comparative finding.

claim: N6mdA was detected in germ-free Drosophila melanogaster at approximately 0.04%.
source: N6mdA was also detected in germ-free D. melanogaster (~0.04%, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The results section states this finding and references a figure.

claim: Adult Drosophila melanogaster contained methylated adenine as a DNA building block.
source: While the adult D. melanogaster contained methylated adenine as a DNA building block, ovarian cells collected from two moth species (T. ni and S. frugiperda) principally contained methylated cytosine as the preferred base modification (0.2 and 0.1%, respectively).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: Ovarian cells from Trichoplusia ni contained 0.2% methylated cytosine.
source: While the adult D. melanogaster contained methylated adenine as a DNA building block, ovarian cells collected from two moth species (T. ni and S. frugiperda) principally contained methylated cytosine as the preferred base modification (0.2 and 0.1%, respectively).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantitative finding.

claim: Ovarian cells from Spodoptera frugiperda contained 0.1% methylated cytosine.
source: While the adult D. melanogaster contained methylated adenine as a DNA building block, ovarian cells collected from two moth species (T. ni and S. frugiperda) principally contained methylated cytosine as the preferred base modification (0.2 and 0.1%, respectively).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantitative finding.

claim: Most vertebrate genomes studied had a 5mdC content of around 5% of the cytosine residues.
source: Most vertebrate genomes studied had a 5mdC content of around 5% (mean 4.66, SD 2.17) of the cytosine residues.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with statistical measures.

claim: In plants, 5mdC concentrations of 10% and higher were typical.
source: In plants, however, 5mdC concentrations of 10% (mean 20.34, SD 9.81) and higher were typical (Figure 1D).
evidence: The results section states this finding with statistical measures and references a figure.

claim: In Andropogon gerardii, more than 35% of cytosines were methylated.
source: Extremely high values for cytosine methylation were observed in Andropogon gerardii and Allium cepa, where more than 35% of cytosines were methylated (Figure 1D, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding and references figures.

claim: In Allium cepa, more than 35% of cytosines were methylated.
source: Extremely high values for cytosine methylation were observed in Andropogon gerardii and Allium cepa, where more than 35% of cytosines were methylated (Figure 1D, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding and references figures.

claim: Most tissues in Garra barreimiae, Marmota marmota, and Mus musculus had 5mdC levels of around 5-6%.
source: For instance, most tissues in G. barreimiae, M. marmota, and M. musculus tissues had 5mdC levels of around 5–6% (Figure 3A).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding and references a figure.

claim: Between different mouse lines, there were no significant differences in 5mdC levels.
source: Between the different mouse lines, there were no significant differences in 5mdC levels (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: Brain tissue had a higher median value for percentage methylation compared to other tissues (5.3 vs. 4.9%).
source: Heart tissue presented a broad cytosine methylation level and brain tissue had a higher median value for percentage methylation compared to other tissues (5.3 vs. 4.9%; Figure 3B).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this comparative finding and references a figure.

claim: 5hmdC was not detected in spleen tissues.
source: Although the spleen tissues had similar 5mdC levels as other mouse tissues, 5hmdC was not detected in these tissues (Figure 3B).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding and references a figure.

claim: The highest 5hmdC levels were detected in the fish Garra barreimiae, where levels could reach up to 8% of cytosine residues.
source: Interestingly, our data reveals that the highest 5hmdC levels were not detected in the mammalian brain, but in the fish G. barreimiae. were levels could reach up to 8% of cytosine residues
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: Mus musculus brain tissue had 3.3% 5hmdC.
source: Although lower compared to G. barreimiae, mammals M. musculus (3.3%), and amphibian X. laevis (2%) still had high levels of 5hmdC specifically in brain tissue relative to other tissues in those organisms (Figure 3A, right).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantitative finding and references a figure.

claim: Xenopus laevis brain tissue had 2% 5hmdC.
source: Although lower compared to G. barreimiae, mammals M. musculus (3.3%), and amphibian X. laevis (2%) still had high levels of 5hmdC specifically in brain tissue relative to other tissues in those organisms (Figure 3A, right).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantitative finding and references a figure.

claim: In opossum, 5hmdC levels were not higher in the brain compared to peripheral tissue.
source: An interesting exception was in opossum, the only vertebrate species analyzed, in which 5hmdC levels were not higher in the brain compared to peripheral tissue.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this exceptional finding.

claim: 5hmdC was observed in Arabidopsis thaliana and Oryza sativa.
source: Apart from vertebrates, 5hmdC was also observed in A. thaliana and Oryza sativa (Mahmood and Dunwell, 2019).
evidence: The results section cites a paper supporting this finding.

claim: 5hmdC was not detected in the majority of plant samples.
source: Our data shows that the presence of 5hmdC is by no means universal in plants, indeed, we did not detect it in the majority of plant samples.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding from the study.

claim: Low concentrations of 5hmdC were confirmed in Allium cepa, Laurus nobilis, Lepidium sativum, and Raphanus sativus.
source: Nonetheless, our data adds several species (A. cepa, Laurus nobilis, Lepidium sativum, and R. sativus) in which we confirmed low concentrations of 5hmdC.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: 5hmdC was not detected in any of the bacterial or fungal genomes analyzed.
source: Furthermore, we did not detect 5hmdC in any of the bacterial or fungal genomes analyzed.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: The highest levels of N6mdA in prokaryotes were detected in Mobiluncus curtisii at approximately 1.4%.
source: In prokaryotes, high amounts of DNA modifications all concerned N6mdA, with the highest levels detected in Mobiluncus curtisii (~1.4%) and Moorell thermoacetica (~1.1%).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantitative finding.

claim: Moorella thermoacetica had approximately 1.1% N6mdA.
source: In prokaryotes, high amounts of DNA modifications all concerned N6mdA, with the highest levels detected in Mobiluncus curtisii (~1.4%) and Moorell thermoacetica (~1.1%).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantitative finding.

claim: Typical bacterial species contain only one type of modification—mostly N6mdA.
source: Typical bacterial species contain only one type of modification—mostly N6mdA (Figure 4A).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding and references a figure.

claim: Certain genera such as Campylobacter contain trace quantities of 5mdC (<0.1%) next to the dominating N6mdA modification.
source: Certain genera such as Campylobacter contain trace quantities of 5mdC (<0.1%) next to the dominating N6mdA modification (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: Mobiluncus curtisii has approximately 1.4% of its adenine residues methylated and shows only 0.3% 5mdC.
source: For instance, M. curtisii with ~1.4% of its adenine residues methylated shows only 0.3% 5mdC
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantitative finding.

claim: Sebaldella termitidis has approximately 2.4% cytosine methylation and only 0.1% of its adenines methylated.
source: while Sebaldella termitidis, with unusually high cytosine methylation (~2.4%), has only 0.1% of its adenines methylated.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantitative finding.

claim: Neisseria gonorrhoeae showed 1.4% of cytosine residues were methylated while containing only <0.3% N6mdA.
source: This included the genus Neisseria, mucosal-surface-colonizing bacteria, which showed 1.4 and 2% (Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Neisseria lactamica, respectively) of cytosine residues were methylated while containing only <0.3% N6mdA
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantitative finding.

claim: Neisseria lactamica showed 2% of cytosine residues were methylated while containing only <0.3% N6mdA.
source: This included the genus Neisseria, mucosal-surface-colonizing bacteria, which showed 1.4 and 2% (Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Neisseria lactamica, respectively) of cytosine residues were methylated while containing only <0.3% N6mdA
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantitative finding.

claim: Faecalicoccus pleomorphus had >1.5% of 5mdC without any detectable levels of N6mdA modification.
source: and Faecalicoccus pleomorphus and Bifidobacterium adolescentis, with >1.5% of 5mdC without any detectable levels of N6mdA modification.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantitative finding.

claim: Bifidobacterium adolescentis had >1.5% of 5mdC without any detectable levels of N6mdA modification.
source: and Faecalicoccus pleomorphus and Bifidobacterium adolescentis, with >1.5% of 5mdC without any detectable levels of N6mdA modification.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantitative finding.

claim: Candida albicans contained 5mdC as the sole yeast species.
source: While the environmental yeasts studied herein and previously lacked any modifications (Capuano et al., 2014), the most frequent commensal yeast pathogen Candida albicans contained as sole yeast species 5mdC (Mishra et al., 2011).
evidence: The results section cites a paper supporting this finding.

claim: 4mdC was detected in tandem with 5mdC in Shewanella putrefaciens, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, Bifidobacterium dentium, Mobiluncus curtisii, and Gallibacterium anatis.
source: Finally, we also observed a third modification, 4mdC, to be frequent in prokaryotes. 4mdC was detected in tandem with 5mdC as a second modification in Shewanella putrefaciens, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, Bifidobacterium dentium, M. curtisii, and Gallibacterium anatis (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, not quantified).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding and references a figure.

claim: No significant correlation was detected between factors such as pathogenicity, temperature of growth, or tolerance to oxygen and the amount of modifications per unit genome size.
source: Similarly, we detected no significant correlation between factors such as pathogenicity, temperature of growth, or tolerance to oxygen and the amount of modifications per unit genome size (not shown).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this negative finding.

claim: No relationship was detected between nature and level of modification with genome size or GC content.
source: We did not detect any relationship between nature and level of modification with genome size or GC content (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this negative finding and references a figure.

claim: Members of the same genus often displayed similar values for a given modification.
source: We did, however, observe obvious patterns at the different taxonomic levels once we grouped the different bacterial strains according to phylum, class, and genus. Similarities are detected at the genus level (Figure 4B, C). Members of the same genus often displayed similar values for a given modification.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding and references figures.

claim: α- and γ-Proteobacteria had the highest N6mdA content among different classes present.
source: At the class level, we observed trends between the different classes and the amount of modification. α- and γ-Proteobacteria had the highest N6mdA content among different classes present while bacteroidetes presented with more cytidine methylation than adenosine methylation.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: Bacteroidetes presented with more cytidine methylation than adenosine methylation.
source: At the class level, we observed trends between the different classes and the amount of modification. α- and γ-Proteobacteria had the highest N6mdA content among different classes present while bacteroidetes presented with more cytidine methylation than adenosine methylation.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: Proteobacteria contained more N6mdA than 5mdC.
source: At the phylum level, the patterns were more prominent in Proteobacteria, containing more N6mdA than 5mdC, while a reverse trend of more 5mdC than N6mdA was observed for Bacteroidetes and Firmicutes.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: Bacteroidetes and Firmicutes showed more 5mdC than N6mdA.
source: At the phylum level, the patterns were more prominent in Proteobacteria, containing more N6mdA than 5mdC, while a reverse trend of more 5mdC than N6mdA was observed for Bacteroidetes and Firmicutes.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

source: DNA extracts were treated with RNase A (VWR, Cat.No. E866-5ML) at 37°C for 45 min
evidence: The methods section explicitly describes this procedural step.

claim: DNA purification was performed using QIAGEN Genomic tip-20/G.
source: and DNA purification was performed using QIAGEN Genomic tip-20/G according to the manufacturer's instructions.
evidence: The methods section explicitly describes this procedural step.

claim: 1 µg of DNA was treated with 5 U of DNA degradase at 37°C for 2 hr.
source: 1 µg of DNA was treated with 5 U of DNA degradase at 37°C for 2 hr in a final volume of 25 μl
evidence: The methods section explicitly describes this procedural step.

claim: The reaction was inactivated by incubating the samples for 20 min at 70°C.
source: and the reaction was inactivated by incubating the samples for 20 min at 70°C as described by the manufacturer.
evidence: The methods section explicitly describes this procedural step.

claim: 10 µl corresponding to 200 ng of gDNA were injected onto the liquid chromatography system.
source: The samples were diluted 1:1 with MeOH 10% (v/v) containing 0.2% formic acid, and 10 µl corresponding to 200 ng of gDNA were injected onto a liquid chromatography system
evidence: The methods section explicitly describes this procedural step.

claim: The column temperature was 25°C and flow rate was 0.2 ml/min.
source: equipped with reverse phase Acquity UPLC HSS T3 column, 100 Å, 1.8 µm, 2.1 mm × 150 mm (Waters), column temperature 25°C and flow rate of 0.2 ml/min.
evidence: The methods section explicitly describes these instrumental parameters.

claim: The LC-MRM method was expanded from a previous method designed for the quantification of 5mdC.
source: In order to quantify the global levels of multiple enzymatic DNA modifications in a single analysis, we expanded a previous method based on liquid chromatography-multiple reaction monitoring (LC-MRM) and designed for the quantification of 5mdC (Tsuji et al., 2014).
evidence: The results section cites a previous method that was expanded.

claim: The method discriminates between RNA and DNA modifications based on the precursor mass difference of the sugar moiety.
source: Distinguishing the nucleosides arising from a DNA monomer from a potentially co-purified RNA monomer occurs on the basis of the precursor mass difference of the sugar moiety.
evidence: The results section explicitly describes this methodological feature.

claim: A neutral loss scan was used as a strategy to confirm the MRM results and to detect additional modifications such as 4mdC.
source: Moreover, we supplemented the method by a neutral loss scan as a strategy to confirm the MRM results, as well as to detect additional modifications such as 4mdC, that were not included among the standards.
evidence: The results section explicitly describes this methodological addition.

claim: No adenosine modification was observed for Sulfolobus acidocaldarius.
source: Our study further featured two archeal genomes (Sulfolobus acidocaldarius and Halobacterium salinarum), which shared a similar level of the cytosine modification but differed in their levels of adenosine modification. While we detected N6mdA in H. salinarum, no adenosine modification was observed for S. acidocaldarius (Supplementary file 1).
